title: Devon blue brook pollution focus of resident survey
summary:
People affected by a pollution incident that turned a brook bright blue are being asked to share their experiences as part of an ongoing investigation.
The Environment Agency has launched a survey following the contamination of Littleham Brook in Exmouth, Devon between 11 and 25 September.
It prompted warnings against swimming and other water activities at Exmouth beach while officials investigated the cause.
Clarissa Newell, regulatory manager at the Environment Agency, said: "We want information from people, businesses and organisations who may have been affected by this incident.
"This could be specifically during this period or you may still be experiencing ongoing impacts."

title: Cutting EV target risks UK missing climate targets, warns adviser
summary:
The UK is likely to miss legally binding climate targets if the government reduces electric vehicle (EV) targets, independent adviser the Climate Change Committee (CCC) has warned.
The CCC says that switching to an electric vehicle can save a typical household around £800 a year, with fewer people benefiting if the targets were watered down.
The warning comes after weeks of speculation that the government plans to announce changes to the EV targets.
Under the current rules, a "zero emission vehicle" (ZEV) mandate requires 80% of new cars sold in the UK to be zero emission by 2030 and all new cars to meet that standard by 2035.
Companies that fail to meet their ZEV mandate face a potential fine of £12,000 per car, although there are exemptions.

title: Powering towns on pig manure: How Denmark has transformed energy generation
summary:
As the world seeks to cut carbon emissions to slow global warming, livestock manure is driving Denmark’s energy transition.
However, Denmark has been engineering a biogas boom, developing facilities to convert livestock waste into renewable natural gas to power the national grid and transport, fuel homes and make fertiliser.
Today, Denmark has Europe’s highest share of biogas in its gas grid, at about 40 percent.

title: Mobuoy: Dump clean-up could cost £161m over 30 years, says environment minister
summary:
More than £160m is needed to clean up and maintain one of Europe's largest illegal landfill sites, government officials have said.
The contaminated Mobuoy dump at Campsie in County Londonderry, discovered and shut down in 2013, was used to bury thousands of tonnes of rubbish at a site spanning more than 100 acres.
Northern Ireland's Environment Minister Andrew Muir said his department had now received an updated cost estimate of £161m for the clean-up over a 30-year period.
Muir described what happened at Mobuoy as "an absolute scandal" and said "the community rightly expects and deserves remediation of the site".
He is now seeking a meeting with the Finance Minister John O'Dowd to discuss how the work will be paid for - with funding from Westminster a possibility.
